items.prompt: A singly linked structure may contain a cycle. The routine must not modify nodes and may use only O(1) extra space. Which strategy directly fits the contract?
constraints: Each node has at most one next reference.
The list must remain unchanged.

options.text: Sort payload values and look for duplicates.
Store every visited node reference in a hash set.
Reverse links and infer a cycle from whether the head changes.
Advance slow by one and fast by two; report a cycle only if their node references meet after movement.

feedback.reason: Floyd's convergence test detects a reachable cycle without mutation or a visited-node collection.

blocks.text: In an acyclic list, fast eventually reaches null. In a reachable cycle, both pointers enter the cycle and their relative position changes until their references coincide. A visited set is correct but uses O(n) extra space; duplicate values do not imply repeated nodes; reversing mutates the structure and does not provide the stated safe contract.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.visited_set: This can detect a cycle but violates the O(1)-extra-space requirement.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.sort_values: Payload duplicates are unrelated to structural cycles and sorting does not expose repeated node identity.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.reverse_structure: Mutation is forbidden, and head changes are not a valid general cycle criterion.

items.prompt: After slow and fast are both inside a cycle of length L, slow advances one edge and fast two per iteration. Why must they eventually reference the same node?
constraints: Both pointers are already inside the same reachable cycle.
The speed difference is exactly one edge per iteration.

options.text: Their relative offset increases by one modulo L, so within at most L iterations it becomes zero.
Fast eventually reaches null inside the cycle and waits for slow.
A finite cycle must contain duplicate payload values, which forces a meeting.
Slow reverses direction when fast passes it.

feedback.reason: Inside the cycle, the relative phase changes by one modulo the finite cycle length and therefore must hit zero.

blocks.text: Number cycle positions modulo L. Each iteration adds two to fast's position and one to slow's, so the offset gains one modulo L. The sequence of offsets visits every residue before repeating, including zero. Zero means both references designate the same node. Payloads may all be distinct, null is unreachable inside the cycle, and neither pointer changes direction.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.values_repeat: Cycle convergence depends on positions and references, not on payload duplication.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.fast_stops: A pointer following next inside a cycle never reaches null.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.slow_moves_backward: Both pointers continue following next in the same direction.

items.prompt: Select all inputs that contain a cycle under the ordinary singly linked definition.
constraints: A cycle is defined by repeated node identity along next traversal.
Only the listed next references exist.

options.text: head = null, so traversal begins with no node.
head = S and S.next = null.
A.next = B and B.next = A.
head = S and S.next = S.

feedback.reason: A self-loop and a two-node back edge repeat a node reference; empty and null-terminated one-node inputs do not.

blocks.text: A cycle exists when repeated next traversal can return to a node already on the same path. S.next = S repeats S immediately, and A -> B -> A repeats A. An empty input has no path, while S -> null terminates. Minimal tests like these distinguish topology rules from assumptions based only on node count.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.empty: With no node and no edge, there is no reachable cycle.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.single_null: The only traversal step reaches null, so no node repeats.

omittedCorrectExplanationsByOptionId.single_self: A self-reference is a valid cycle of length one.
omittedCorrectExplanationsByOptionId.two_back: The path returns to A after two edges, forming a cycle of length two.

items.prompt: A fresh dummy node is created with dummy.next = head. No data node points to dummy, and no existing data-node next reference is changed. How does starting cycle detection at dummy affect the truth of 'a reachable cycle exists'?
constraints: dummy is newly allocated and has no incoming data-node edge.
All original next references remain unchanged.

options.text: It removes any cycle because dummy itself was not in the original list.
It always creates a cycle because dummy points into the list.
It preserves the answer: dummy adds an acyclic prefix before the same reachable data path.
The answer depends on whether dummy.value duplicates a data value.

feedback.reason: A one-way sentinel prefix does not alter any data-node cycle or create a path back to itself.

blocks.text: Reachability from dummy enters exactly the same path formerly reached from head after one extra edge. If that path terminates, it still terminates; if it enters a cycle, it still enters that cycle. A cycle involving dummy would require a reachable back edge to dummy, which is explicitly absent. Payload values are irrelevant. The sentinel may change pointer phase, but not the existence truth under these conditions.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.always_creates_cycle: An outgoing edge alone is not a cycle; a path must return to an earlier node.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.always_removes_cycle: Prepending a node does not break any existing next edge inside the data path.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.depends_on_dummy_value: Cycle existence is structural and does not depend on duplicate payload values.

items.prompt: For a reachable singly linked component containing at most n distinct nodes before termination or repetition, Floyd's cycle-existence phase follows next with slow and fast. What are its worst-case time and extra-space complexities?
constraints: n counts distinct reachable nodes before null or repetition.
No auxiliary visited collection or skip-link index is used.

feedback.reason: Each pointer follows ordinary next edges, and termination or convergence occurs after O(n) such progress with constant pointer state.

blocks.text: Moving fast two links per iteration changes only a constant factor. It is not binary search because no indexed half is discarded and every jump is implemented as ordinary next dereferences. The acyclic prefix plus at most one cycle's relative-phase convergence is O(n). slow and fast use O(1) extra space; a visited set alternative would use O(n).

items.prompt: An acyclic list is A(value=1) -> B(value=2) -> C(value=1) -> null. A detector reports a cycle when it sees value 1 for the second time. What is the defect?
constraints: A and C are separately allocated nodes.
The list ends at null.

options.text: It should advance the value comparison pointer three nodes at a time.
It should classify null as the cycle entry.
It confuses a repeated payload with revisiting the same node object.
It omitted a sentinel before A.

feedback.reason: A and C are distinct nodes, so duplicate value 1 does not imply repeated traversal state.

blocks.text: The path visits A, B, and C once each and then terminates. A payload may repeat in an acyclic list or be unique throughout a cycle. Correct cycle detectors track node references, either implicitly through fast/slow convergence or explicitly in an identity-based visited set. Sentinel use and step count do not repair a value-based criterion.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.fast_too_slow: No speed can make payload equality a valid structural identity test.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.needs_dummy: A sentinel does not distinguish equal-valued nodes or create a valid cycle signal.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.null_is_cycle: Null is the termination marker for an acyclic singly linked path, not a node in a cycle.

items.prompt: slow and fast both initialize to head. Order one detection-loop iteration so a nonempty acyclic list is not declared cyclic merely because of initialization.
constraints: slow and fast are initialized to the same head reference.
The input may be acyclic and nonempty.

elements.text: Confirm fast and fast.next are not null.
Using the validated pre-update state, advance slow by one link and fast by two links.
Compare slow and fast by node reference and report a cycle if equal.

feedback.reason: The meeting comparison must evaluate positions produced by a valid traversal step, not the intentionally equal initial state.

items: Check `fast != null && fast.next != null`; short-circuit evaluation makes the two-link fast update safe.
From that validated pre-update state, compute `slow = slow.next` and `fast = fast.next.next`.
Compare the resulting node references; equality now means the moving pointers converged.

blocks.text: Comparing before movement would label every nonempty input cyclic because slow and fast intentionally start equal. The two assignments have no required order when both right-hand sides use the pre-update state, so they are one logical step rather than an artificial ordering dependency. Formulations that initialize the pointers at different offsets need their own explicit guard and proof.

items.prompt: Floyd's first phase finds a node M where slow and fast meet. The requested output is the first node E of the cycle, not merely a boolean. Which statement is correct?
constraints: The first Floyd phase has already produced a valid reference meeting M.
The cycle is reachable from head.

options.text: Adding a dummy makes the dummy node the cycle entry.
E is whichever cycle node has the smallest payload value.
M proves a cycle exists, but locating E requires the standard additional phase with one pointer reset to head.
M is always E, so returning M is sufficient.

feedback.reason: The first meeting can occur anywhere in the cycle; the entry follows from a second equal-speed phase using the established distance relation.

blocks.text: Let μ be the number of edges from head to entry E, λ the cycle length, and m the number of cycle edges from E to the first meeting M. At that meeting slow has traveled t = μ + m edges, while fast has traveled 2t. Their distance difference is t, and meeting on the cycle means t = kλ for some integer k. Therefore μ + m = kλ, so μ edges forward from M land at E after completing the remaining whole-cycle distance.

items: Keep one pointer at M and reset the other pointer to head.
Advance both pointers one edge per iteration.
After μ steps, the pointer from head reaches E and the pointer from M also reaches E, so their next reference meeting is the cycle entry.

blocks.text: Thus M proves existence but is not generally E; its location depends on μ and λ. Payload ordering and adding a one-way sentinel do not determine entry identity.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.m_always_entry: The first meeting position varies with prefix and cycle lengths and is not generally the entry.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.compare_values_for_entry: Cycle entry is a topological position, not a payload minimum.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.dummy_is_entry: A one-way sentinel predecessor lies before the data path and does not become a member of the existing cycle.

items.prompt: After Floyd's slow and fast pointers meet inside a cycle, how can the first cycle-entry node be found?

options.text: Reset one pointer to head, then advance both one step at a time; their next meeting is the cycle entry.
Return the first meeting node because it is always the cycle entry.
Reset fast to head and keep moving it twice as fast until it passes slow.
Sort node values to identify where the cycle begins.

feedback.reason: The phase relation at the first meeting lets a head pointer and meeting pointer converge at the entry under equal speed.

blocks.text: The first meeting proves a cycle exists but may occur after the entry. Reset one pointer to head and move both one link per iteration; the distance relation modulo the cycle length makes their next meeting the first cycle node. Values are irrelevant to structural identity.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.return_meeting: The meeting point can be anywhere within the cycle.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.restart_fast_two: Keeping unequal speeds does not implement the entry-recovery phase.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.sort_values: Cycle structure is defined by next references, not node values.

items.prompt: Which guard is required before advancing fast by two links in a singly linked cycle detector?

options.text: Check fast is non-null and fast.next is non-null before evaluating fast = fast.next.next.
Check only slow because fast is always ahead and therefore non-null.
Read fast.next.next first and check the result afterward.
Check node values for a sentinel instead of pointer nullability.

feedback.reason: Both dereferences in a two-link advance need a valid predecessor pointer.

blocks.text: On an acyclic list, fast may be null or point to the final node whose next is null. The short-circuit guard must run before either dereference. Pointer values, not payload values, define termination and cycle truth.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.slow_only: Fast can reach null independently of slow.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.next_next_only: Reading through a null fast or fast.next already fails before the check.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.value_guard: A valid node may contain any value and nullability is a pointer property.

items.prompt: After Floyd's pointers meet, what transformation finds the cycle entry?
constraints: The list contains a cycle.
The meeting node is inside that cycle.

options.text: Reset one pointer to head, then advance both one link at a time until they meet again.
options.explanation: This equalizes the distance relation needed to locate the entry.

options.text: Keep one pointer moving two links and stop at the first repeated value.
options.explanation: The second phase relies on equal one-link speeds and node identity, not payload repetition.

options.text: Sort the reachable nodes by address before searching for the entry.
options.explanation: Sorting does not preserve or expose cycle topology.

options.text: Restart both pointers at head and move them at their original unequal speeds.
options.explanation: The phase relation requires one pointer to start at the meeting point and both to move one link.

feedback.reason: The meeting proves existence; the reset-and-equal-speed phase uses the modular distance relation to identify the first cycle node.

blocks.text: Once the pointers meet, the distance from head to entry matches the distance from the meeting point around the cycle after accounting for a whole cycle length. Moving one pointer from head and the other from the meeting point at equal speed makes their next meeting the entry. Value equality or sorting is unrelated to pointer topology.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.keep_fast_speed: The second phase relies on equal one-link speeds and node identity, not payload repetition.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.sort_nodes: Sorting does not preserve or expose cycle topology.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.restart_both_head: The phase relation requires one pointer to start at the meeting point and both to move one link.

items.prompt: Which boundary case must a cycle detector classify as cyclic even though the node has no distinct predecessor?
constraints: A single node points to itself.
The detector compares node references.

options.text: The single self-loop is a cycle; the node is both the entry and the meeting location.
options.explanation: A cycle is defined by reachability returning to the same node, including length one.

options.text: A one-node list is always acyclic because there is no second node.
options.explanation: Cycle length one is valid when next points back to the node.

options.text: Classify by whether the payload equals a reserved sentinel value.
options.explanation: Payload values do not determine pointer cycles.

options.text: Require two distinct meeting nodes before returning true.
options.explanation: One reference meeting is sufficient evidence in Floyd's detector.

feedback.reason: A self-loop satisfies the structural definition of a cycle and must not be excluded by a length-based assumption.

blocks.text: The detector should test links, not the number of distinct nodes. With head.next === head, slow and fast converge at the only node. Requiring two nodes or two meetings rejects a legal cycle.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.single_node_acyclic: Cycle length one is valid when next points back to the node.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.value_sentinel: Payload values do not determine pointer cycles.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.require_two_meetings: One reference meeting is sufficient evidence in Floyd's detector.

items.prompt: Why does Floyd's cycle detector satisfy an O(1) auxiliary-space contract while still making linear-time progress?
constraints: The list exposes only next links.
The algorithm stores a constant number of node references.

options.text: It stores only fixed pointers and advances through each phase; the number of stored references does not grow with n.
options.explanation: Constant pointer state is the space guarantee.

options.text: It stores every visited node in a hash set, which is constant space.
options.explanation: A visited set grows with the number of nodes.

options.text: It uses random access to skip nodes without storing them.
options.explanation: Singly linked lists do not provide random access.

options.text: The two pointer speeds imply logarithmic auxiliary memory.
options.explanation: Pointer speed affects time, not storage growth.

feedback.reason: The algorithm trades a small constant pointer state for repeated traversal and convergence.

blocks.text: Floyd's method keeps slow, fast, and phase variables only. It may traverse a linear number of links, but no visited collection or recursion depth proportional to the list is allocated.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.visited_set: A visited set grows with the number of nodes.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.random_access: Singly linked lists do not provide random access.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.logarithmic_memory: Pointer speed affects time, not storage growth.

items.prompt: Acyclic list contains repeated payload values. Why must a cycle detector compare node identity rather than payload equality?
constraints: Different nodes may contain equal values.
A cycle is a property of next-link reachability.

options.text: Equal payloads on distinct nodes are not a cycle; only the same node reference reached again proves convergence.
options.explanation: Topology is represented by references, not payload values.

options.text: The first repeated payload marks the cycle entry.
options.explanation: Repeated values can occur in a completely acyclic list.

options.text: Linked-list nodes are structurally required to have unique payloads.
options.explanation: Payload uniqueness is not a linked-list invariant.

options.text: Compare numeric positions instead of references because positions are stable under traversal.
options.explanation: A singly linked list does not expose stable indices without additional bookkeeping.

feedback.reason: Cycle truth is an aliasing relation on node objects, not a value relation.

blocks.text: Repeated values are legal and do not imply that traversal returned to an earlier node. Reference equality directly observes whether two pointers designate the same object; payload comparisons can create false positives.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.first_duplicate_cycle: Repeated values can occur in a completely acyclic list.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.unique_payload_assumption: Payload uniqueness is not a linked-list invariant.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.compare_positions: A singly linked list does not expose stable indices without additional bookkeeping.
